title: A finite separable field extension has a primitive element
statement: Let $F\subseteq E$ be a finite separable extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then there is $\alpha\in E$ such that $E=F(\alpha)$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 030N (lemma-primitive-element), the moreover clause for separable finite extensions

mathlib_searches.query: finite separable field extension has a primitive element

mathlib_searches.results: exists_primitive_element under [FiniteDimensional F E] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E]

mathlib_match.how: Under [FiniteDimensional F E] and [Algebra.IsSeparable F E], the declaration gives alpha with F⟮balpha⟩ = top, exactly E = F(alpha).
